Goal: I can find an angle from a ratio.

slides.title: The big idea
slides.html:
Inverse trig finds an angle from a ratio. If tan A = 0.75, then A = tan−1(0.75), about 36.9 degrees. Likewise sin−1 and cos−1.

tan−1 means "the angle whose tangent is," not 1 divided by tan.

The ADA standard for a ramp is a slope of at most 1 : 12. The angle is tan−1(1/12), about 4.76 degrees, so a ramp steeper than about 4.8 degrees fails the code.

slides.title: Check yourself
slides.html: A ramp rises 0.5 m over a horizontal run of 5 m. Does it meet the 1 : 12 rule? Find its angle.
slides.reveal: Slope 0.5/5 = 1/10 is steeper than 1/12, so it fails. Angle = tan^−1(0.1), about 5.7 degrees.
